title: From land to cup
disclaimer: A fictional, simulated coffee journey for learning about FoaMES. Sources explain the process; they do not supply this demo's production data. No producer affiliation, live equipment connection, or food-safety certification is implied.

stages.title: Land and soil
stages.subtitle: Start with a place and its evidence
stages.summary: Map a fictional plot, assess drainage and access, and review soil and water evidence before establishing the orchard. Keep the land assessment linked to every later harvest.
controls: Drainage, water availability and access review
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: land suitability and soil management

stages.title: Seeds and nursery
stages.subtitle: Preserve identity as plants grow
stages.summary: Follow a seed lot into a nursery cohort and then into planted rows. Record variety, supplier, germination and plant health so the orchard retains its origin story.
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: seed quality and nursery establishment

stages.title: Trellis establishment
stages.subtitle: Explore the selected cultivation method
stages.summary: This scenario selects the Kona Joe-inspired method of training coffee shoots along wires into horizontal cordons. Track installation, training and pruning. No yield or flavor advantage is assumed.

stages.title: Cultivation
stages.subtitle: Observe the orchard through the season
stages.summary: Connect field observations, water use, plant health and maintenance to the plot. A finding prompts a person to review the evidence and choose an action.
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: cultivation, water and plant health

stages.title: Cherry harvest
stages.subtitle: Turn a crop into a traceable lot
stages.summary: Assign the picked cherries a harvest lot with plot, date, maturity sample and measured mass. Keep rejected fruit visible and preserve the time between picking and processing.
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: ripeness and selective harvesting

stages.title: Wet processing
stages.subtitle: Separate fruit, seed and byproducts
stages.summary: Follow the selected washed route through pulping, monitored mucilage removal and washing. Link inputs and outputs, including pulp and wastewater, rather than hiding them inside one yield number.
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: fermentation and water-efficient processing

stages.title: Drying and conditioning
stages.subtitle: Measure readiness for storage
stages.summary: Track drying conditions and sampled moisture before releasing parchment for storage. Keep sample identity and instrument checks with the result; water removed is different from rejected coffee.
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: drying, moisture and storage stability

stages.title: Green coffee and receiving
stages.subtitle: Keep quality and custody together
stages.summary: Hull, sort and identify the green lot, then reconcile dispatch with receipt at the roastery. Review the sample and storage evidence before the lot becomes available to a roast job.
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: grading, storage and transport

stages.title: Roasting and cooling
stages.subtitle: A batch, a profile and a human release
stages.summary: Match a roast job to equipment capacity and a reviewed recipe. Follow the temperature trace, machine states, charge and discharge mass, cooling and sensory review as one batch history.
controls: Roast profile, cooling and mass loss
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: roast development and sensory quality

stages.title: Packaging and dispatch
stages.subtitle: Carry the lot through every pack
stages.summary: Connect the roast batch to package lots and shipments. A failed check creates a visible hold; reviewed evidence is required before the affected lot is released.
controls: Fill mass, seal and lot-label checks
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: packaging, oxygen and shelf life

stages.title: Grinding and brewing
stages.subtitle: Connect the recipe to the cup
stages.summary: Trace the package lot into a measured dose and brew run. Record water, beverage output, grind, time, temperature and dissolved solids against the selected method's recipe.
controls: Beverage mass, dissolved solids and sensory result
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: grinding, extraction and consumer preferences

stages.title: Cup delivery
stages.subtitle: Close the journey with a handoff
stages.summary: Connect an order to its brew and record the cup handoff. Trace backward to the plot or forward from a held lot to affected cups. A prepared cup is not counted as delivered until its handoff is recorded.
stages.paper_status: Papers welcome: service quality and delivery

sources.title: Gaggia Classic Pro RI9380 operating instructions
sources.locator: RI9380 (SIN035R), November 2022 revision; Fig. 1 and component description
sources.claim: Identifies the Classic Pro's power, brew and steam controls, filter holder, steam wand, water tank and drip tray; used as a reference for the original schematic illustration.
sources.limitations: The CLR powder-coated finish and external PID are fictional customizations. The model does not reproduce measured Gaggia thermal dynamics or newer Classic variants. No manufacturer affiliation is implied.

sources.title: Classic PIDs?
sources.locator: May 30, 2022; discussion of Classic thermostats and PID modifications
sources.claim: Describes thermostat-based temperature control and discusses PID modifications on the Classic models of that period.
sources.limitations: Historical distributor commentary, not a retrofit design or a statement about all current Classic variants. The demo provides no installation, tuning or machine certification.

sources.title: CLR website color palette
sources.locator: CSS design tokens at the existing website revision
sources.claim: Defines CLR blue #3683A4 and olive #A2A342 with mist, ink and sky supporting colors.
sources.limitations: Digital color reference for the illustrative powder-coat concept, not a physical coating specification or exact printed color match.

sources.title: Growing Coffee in Hawaii
sources.publisher: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, CTAHR
sources.locator: March 2008 revision; printed pp. 3–17 and 32–39
sources.claim: Covers site assessment, nursery establishment, cultivation, harvesting, wet processing, drying, hulling and grading.
sources.limitations: Historical Hawaii guidance. Local agronomy and current requirements need separate review; this demo does not adopt its fertilizer, pesticide or operating recipes.

sources.title: Good Practice Guide: Seed Producers
sources.locator: Guide overview and supporting traceability tables
sources.claim: Provides resources for coffee seed production and traceability.
sources.limitations: The landing page and resource descriptions were reviewed. The full technical manual was not reviewed for this demo.

sources.title: Good Practice Guide: Coffee Nursery Management
sources.locator: Guide overview and supporting traceability tables
sources.claim: Provides nursery-management guidance and traceability resources for producing quality planting material.
sources.limitations: The landing page was reviewed. The full PDF exceeded the research tool's size limit; no detailed nursery prescription is inferred.

sources.title: What Makes Us Different?
sources.locator: An Innovative Process
sources.claim: The producer describes horizontal cordons, managed vertical growth and maturity observations including pH, sugar concentration and titratable acidity.
sources.limitations: Producer-reported practices and benefits, not independent comparative evidence. The demo has no producer affiliation and applies no yield or flavor uplift. Independent trellis paper pending.

sources.title: US6449898B1: Method and apparatus for enhancing coffee bean production
sources.publisher: US patent publication; inventor Joseph B. Alban
sources.locator: Published September 17, 2002; abstract and detailed description
sources.claim: Describes a coffee trellis with posts and wires, attachment of growing shoots, and optional drip irrigation.
sources.limitations: Documents an invention rather than independently validating agronomic results. No legal-status conclusion or implementation license is asserted. Independent research paper pending.

sources.title: Kona Joe Self Guided Tour
sources.locator: The Trellised Coffee Tree and subsequent wet-processing description
sources.claim: Describes the producer's hand harvesting, pulping, washing and drying sequence.
sources.limitations: Tour and marketing material. Its reported production increase is not used as a demo parameter or an independently established benefit.

sources.title: Coffee Berry Borer: How Can We Manage It?
sources.publisher: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, CTAHR
sources.locator: Damage and integrated management sections
sources.claim: Describes coffee berry borer damage and the role of integrated management.
sources.limitations: Used to motivate scouting and evidence records. Treatment decisions require current local guidance; no automatic treatment or loss forecast is derived.

sources.title: Measuring Coffee Bean Moisture Content
sources.publisher: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, CTAHR
sources.locator: EN-3, March 2008; pp. 1–3
sources.claim: Explains why coffee moisture matters for quality and traded mass, and discusses measurement and calibration.
sources.limitations: Historical guidance. Demo moisture limits are illustrative site specifications, not a claim about current legal grading limits.

sources.title: A comprehensive analysis of operations and mass flows in postharvest processing of washed coffee
sources.publisher: Rotta et al.; Resources, Conservation and Recycling, 2021
sources.locator: Volume 170, article 105554; abstract and UC Davis Coffee Center author-institution summary
sources.claim: Examines washed-coffee operations and material flows from harvest to consumption, including byproducts.
sources.limitations: Abstract and institutional summary reviewed; publisher full text was inaccessible. Study averages are not this fictional lot's yields. Consumed coffee solids are distinct from beverage mass.

sources.title: Modern Marvels: How Coffee is Made
sources.locator: 00:56–03:13; receiving, cleaning, roasting and cooling
sources.claim: Presents an industrial example of receiving coffee, removing foreign material and running roast batches.
sources.limitations: Based on exported English captions, not visual inspection. Captions may contain errors. Historical documentary figures are examples, not current facility data or operating instructions.

sources.title: Production Facility Tour: Green Coffee and Incoming Quality
sources.locator: 01:27–03:09; sorting, storage, sample roasting and cupping
sources.claim: Describes green-bean sorting and incoming quality evaluation before production.
sources.limitations: Based on exported auto-generated English captions, not visual inspection. Captions contain transcription errors. Producer statements are not independent verification or demo production measurements.

sources.title: Production Facility Tour: Roasting and Quality
sources.locator: 03:10–04:39; roaster selection, sensors and quality review
sources.claim: Describes matching batch size to roasters, monitoring the roast and stopping production when quality is out of specification.
sources.limitations: Based on exported auto-generated English captions, not visual inspection. Captions contain transcription errors. Equipment capacities and sensor counts are producer-reported examples, not demo parameters.

sources.title: Production Facility Tour: Packaging Checks
sources.locator: 04:40–05:40; dissolved solids, package oxygen and form-fill-seal packaging
sources.claim: Describes product and packaging quality checks alongside automated filling and packaging.
sources.limitations: Based on exported auto-generated English captions, not visual inspection. Captions contain transcription errors. Packaging settings, rates and material claims are not independently verified.

sources.title: Production Facility Tour: Retained Samples
sources.locator: 00:48–01:26; retained production samples and complaint investigation
sources.claim: Describes retaining samples to investigate package integrity and complaints.
sources.limitations: Based on exported auto-generated English captions, not visual inspection. Captions contain transcription errors. The producer's retention practice is not a universal retention requirement.

sources.title: Coffee Value Assessment Standards
sources.locator: Published standards: SCA-102, SCA-103, SCA-104 and SCA-105
sources.claim: Distinguishes sample preparation and tasting mechanics, descriptive assessment, affective assessment and extrinsic assessment.
sources.limitations: The public standards overview was reviewed. Demo samples and scores are simulated; the demo does not claim SCA certification or complete implementation of these standards.

sources.title: Coffee Brewing Research
sources.locator: Brew temperature, at fixed brew strength and extraction, has little impact on the sensory profile of drip brew coffee; consumer-preference research
sources.claim: Reports interactions among brew strength, extraction and sensory outcomes. Temperature alone does not determine quality in the studied drip-brew conditions.
sources.limitations: Institutional summaries reviewed. Findings are limited to the studied methods and conditions; the demo does not predict flavor or prescribe a universally preferred cup.

sources.title: Certification Standards: Brewers
sources.locator: Scope, brewing time and brewing temperature
sources.claim: Specifies method-dependent testing of filter and fresh-brew machines, including time, grind and temperature measurements.
sources.limitations: Its scope excludes manual pour-over, French press, espresso and pod/capsule machines. It does not establish a safe serving temperature or certify this demo.

sources.title: FoaMES Coffee Demo: Order and Cup Handoff
sources.locator: Coffee example catalog and replay
sources.claim: Uses explicit order, brew and handoff events to demonstrate traceability through cup delivery.
sources.limitations: A fictional operational design, not a published service standard. Timestamps, customer orders and outcomes are simulated.
